summary: Your mind races against itself. Ideas fire faster than you can sort them, so you blurt, you provoke, you change your position mid-sentence. Brilliant and scattered live in the same head.
body: Your mind races against itself. Ideas fire faster than you can sort them, so you blurt, you provoke, you change your position mid-sentence. Brilliant and scattered live in the same head. You may argue for the thrill of it, or get attached to being right for the wrong reasons. That friction is the engine you run on; it makes you quick, inventive, hard to fool. The work is grounding the lightning, giving the ideas a structure before you fire them off.
gift: At your best: quick, inventive, impossible to fool.
shadow: The trap: blurting, provoking, and being right for the wrong reasons.
integration: Let your mind move fast, then give the idea a second pass. Translation is not dilution; it is how the insight becomes useful.
do: Ground the idea before you fire it
Argue to find truth, not to win
